questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

👉 Replace the blanks with “would have secured / would have increased”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Mixed Conditional (Present Unreal Condition → Past Result)

Structure: If + Past Simple (were), would have + V3

This structure is used when a present hypothetical situation is imagined to have produced a different result in the past.

💢 Application to the Given Question - “were” indicates an unreal present condition (Second Conditional structure).

last year - This is a clear past time marker. Therefore, the result clause must refer to a past outcome.

✅ Corrected Sentence - If the company were strategically better positioned, it would have secured the acquisition deal last year and would have increased market share substantially.

Example 1 ✅ - If she were more disciplined, she would have cleared the exam last year.

Example 2 ✅ - If the policy were clearer, investors would have responded positively during the downturn.

Example 3 ✅ - If the bank were financially stronger, it would have avoided losses in the previous quarter.

questions.solution_en:

Rule / Concept: Comparative Degree – Use of “any other”.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The shopkeeper said, "This is the best laptop available in the market."
questions.q_hi:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The shopkeeper said, "This is the best laptop available in the market."
options_en: The shopkeeper said that this was the best laptop available in the market.
The shopkeeper said that it was the best laptop available in the market.
The shopkeeper said that that was the best laptop available in the market.
The shopkeeper said that this is the best laptop available in the market.
options_hi: The shopkeeper said that this was the best laptop available in the market.
The shopkeeper said that it was the best laptop available in the market.
The shopkeeper said that that was the best laptop available in the market.
The shopkeeper said that this is the best laptop available in the market.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option C: The shopkeeper said that that was the best laptop available in the market.

Key Points

  • The "That That" Structure:

    • The first "that" is the conjunction used to connect the reporting verb ("said") to the reported speech.

    • The second "that" is the demonstrative pronoun that replaces the word "this" from the original direct speech.

  • Reporting Verb: The reporting verb "said" is in the Past Tense.

  • Tense Shift: Because the reporting verb is in the past, the verb "is" in the direct speech must be converted to "was" in the indirect speech.

  • Eliminating Incorrect Options:

    • Option A is incorrect because "this" should have been converted to "that".

    • Option B is incorrect because it changes this into it instead of that

    • Option D is incorrect because it fails both the pronoun conversion and the tense shift.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The management is actively seeking an experienced marketing
executive who he can represent the company at
the upcoming international trade summit in Delhi.
No Error
options_hi: The management is actively seeking an experienced marketing
executive who he can represent the company at
the upcoming international trade summit in Delhi.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “who he can” with “who can”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Redundancy of the Personal Pronoun (The Double Subject)

A Relative Pronoun (who, which, that, whom) serves two purposes:

-It acts as a conjunction joining two clauses.

-It acts as a pronoun replacing the noun (antecedent) in the second clause.

When the relative pronoun is used as the subject of the subordinate clause, you must not use another personal pronoun (he, she, it, they) for the same verb. Doing so creates a "double subject" error

Application to the Given Question

"...marketing executive who he can represent the company..."

-Antecedent: Marketing executive

-Relative Pronoun: Who (refers back to the executive)

-Verb: Can represent

In this structure, "who" is already the subject of the verb "can represent." Adding "he" is redundant because both words are trying to perform the same function for the same verb. It is like saying, "Rajat he is going to Delhi."

Corrected Sentence - The management is actively seeking an experienced marketing executive who can represent the company at the upcoming international trade summit in Delhi.

More Examples for Clarity

-Example 1: The book which it is on the table is mine. ❌

-Correction: The book which is on the table is mine. ✅

-Example 2: Those people who they work hard succeed in life. ❌

-Correction: Those people who work hard succeed in life. ✅

-Example 3: This is the car that it broke down yesterday. ❌

-Correction: This is the car that broke down yesterday. ✅

questions.q_en:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The Three Musketeers _______ often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

The Three Musketeers _______ often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.
options_en: were
is
was
be
options_hi: were
is
was
be
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B). Replace the blank with "is".

Rule/Concept: Titles as Abstract Singular Entities:

In English, names of books, movies, countries, or organizations are treated as singular proper nouns. Even if the title contains a plural noun (Musketeers) or a number (Three), it represents one single entity (one story).

The "Article A" Anchor: In complex sentences, look for the phrase "a prime example." The use of the singular article "a" later in the sentence is a dead giveaway that the subject must be singular.

Proper Noun Identification: Words that are capitalized in the middle of a sentence (The Three Musketeers) are usually titles. Treat them as a single "IT," not "THEY."

Common Traps: Watch out for similar titles like Gulliver's Travels, Hard Times, The Arabian Nights, or The United Nations. All of these take a singular verb.

Elimination Strategy: If you see a singular complement (like "a prime example"), immediately eliminate all plural verb options.

Why "Was" (Option C) is incorrect here: If you choose "was," you are implying that the book used to be cited as an example in the past, but it is no longer considered one today. Since the literary status of a masterpiece is usually a continuous fact, the present tense "is" is the grammatically superior choice.

Adverbs of Frequency: Words like "often," "usually," "generally," and "always" are strong signals that the examiner is testing you on the Simple Present Tense.

Correct Sentence: The Three Musketeers is often cited as a prime example of historical romanticism in French literature.

questions.q_en: The data has been verified by the external auditors, ______?
questions.q_hi: The data has been verified by the external auditors, ______?
options_en: hasn’t it
didn’t it
doesn’t it
isn’t it
options_hi: hasn’t it
didn’t it
doesn’t it
isn’t it
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) - “hasn’t it”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Perfect (Passive Voice) + Auxiliary Repetition

When a sentence is in the present perfect tense, especially in passive voice, the auxiliary verb (has / have) must be repeated in the question tag.

If the statement is positive → the tag must be negative.

💢 Application to the Given Question

  • Tense = Present Perfect (Passive)

  • Auxiliary used = has

  • Subject = data (treated as singular in modern exam English) → it

  • Statement is positive → tag must be negative

Therefore: hasn’t it?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ - The report has been finalized, hasn’t it?

Example 2 ✅ - The proposal has been rejected, hasn’t it?

Example 3 ✅ - The agreement has been signed, hasn’t it?

🧠 Things to Remember

  • In passive perfect structures → repeat has/have.

  • Do not shift to “did” unless the sentence is in simple past.

  • In SSC exams, “data” is usually treated as singular → use it.

  • Always identify the first auxiliary in the verb phrase.

👉 Replace “would like to have thanked” with “would have liked to thank”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Use of “Would have liked” for Past Regret / Unfulfilled Intention

“Would like” is used for present polite intention.
“Would have liked” is used to express a past desire or intention that could not be fulfilled.

Structure: Subject + would have liked + to + base verb

When the intention was in the past and not completed, we use would have liked, not would like to have + V3 in formal exam-standard English.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The sentence refers to a past situation (before the board reviewed the documentation).
So the intention existed in the past but was not fulfilled. Therefore, the correct structure is: “would have liked to thank”

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅- She would have liked to attend the interview, but she was out of town.

Example 2 ✅ - The manager would have liked to discuss the proposal earlier.

options_en: Of the two
architectural designs presented,
this one is the better
No Error
options_hi: Of the two
architectural designs presented,
this one is the better
No Error
questions.solution_en:
Rule / Concept: 'The' + Comparative for Selection –

While the definite article 'the' is traditionally associated with superlative degrees (e.g., the best), it is also used with a comparative degree when the sentence involves a selection between exactly two people or things. This usage is typically triggered by the phrase "of the two".

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

Look for "Of the two": This is your strongest signal to use "the" with a comparative adjective.

Comparison vs. Selection: Comparison: He is stronger than his brother (No 'the').

Selection: He is the stronger of the two brothers (Requires 'the').

"The new insolvency regulations concern all major credit-lending institutions in the country."
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the following sentence.

"The new insolvency regulations concern all major credit-lending institutions in the country."
options_en: All major credit-lending institutions in the country are concerned by the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country are concerned with the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country are being concerned by the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country were concerned with the new insolvency regulations.
options_hi: All major credit-lending institutions in the country are concerned by the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country are concerned with the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country are being concerned by the new insolvency regulations.
All major credit-lending institutions in the country were concerned with the new insolvency regulations.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Transitive Verb “Concern” – Passive Formation
When “concern” is used as a transitive verb meaning “affect” or “relate to,” it can form a passive construction in the simple present tense. The structure becomes: Object + is/am/are + V³ (+ by + Subject). The tense must remain unchanged during conversion. Note that “concerned with” carries a different meaning (“involved with”) and is not the passive of “concern” in this context.

The new insolvency regulations concern all major credit-lending institutions in the country. 👉 Replace “In case if” with “In case” or “If”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Redundancy / Superfluous Expressions

In formal English grammar, redundancy occurs when two words or phrases with the same meaning are used together. Both "In case" and "If" are conjunctions used to introduce a condition or a contingency. Using them simultaneously creates a "superfluous" error because one word makes the other unnecessary.

In case: Used to talk about precautions (doing something because something else might happen).

If: Used to talk about a condition (doing something only if something else happens).

✅ Corrected Sentence

In case it rains, I will take an umbrella. (OR)

If it rains, I will take an umbrella.

❌ Incorrect Usage

Wrong example 1 ❌: Suppose if you win the lottery, how will you spend the money?

Wrong example 2 ❌: We will stay indoors in case if the storm gets worse.

No passive is possible because 'run' is an intransitive verb.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Perfect – Active to Passive Conversion
In the Present Perfect tense, the active structure is: Subject + has/have + V³ + Object. The passive structure becomes: Object + has/have + been + V³ (+ by + Subject). The word “been” is mandatory in perfect passive constructions. The main verb must remain in its past participle (V³) form.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The analyst has run a comprehensive simulation of the market crash. Here, “has run” is in the present perfect tense. “A comprehensive simulation of the market crash” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since it is singular, the correct auxiliary is “has.” The correct passive structure is: has + been + run. Option (B) is incorrect because “ran” is the past tense, not the past participle. Option (C) shifts the tense to simple past. Option (D) is incorrect because “run” is transitive in this context (it takes an object).

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

For present perfect passive, use: has/have + been + V³. Do not replace the past participle with the simple past form. Ensure the verb is transitive before forming passive. Maintain the original tense carefully.
